newsitem.title: FRANCE: French activity to pick up in 2nd half 1996-INSEE.
newsitem.headline: French activity to pick up in 2nd half 1996-INSEE.

text.p: French economic activity is expected to pick up in the second half of 1996, boosted by stock-building and low interest rates, national statistics institute INSEE said on Friday.
But it said that overall gross domestic product (GDP) growth in 1996 would be 1.2 percent, slightly less than the government's official forecast of 1.3 percent.

"In the second half, activity should pick up, stimulated by stock-building, the low level of interest rates compensating the negative effect of measures to straighten out the budget," INSEE said in its semi-annual economic note.
It said growth should be 1.0 percent in the third quarter compared with the previous quarter and 0.4 percent in the fourth.
"This irregular progress is due to seasonal effects and to strong car buying in August and September."
In the first quarter output rose 1.1 percent before falling 0.4 percent in the second quarter.
In the second half of this year, the French economy should be growing at an annualised rate of over 2.0 percent compared with about 1.0 percent in the first half, it said.

The conservative government is counting on a recovery in the second half continuing into next year to produce growth of 2.3 percent in 1997, in order to meet its targets for reducing the budget deficit ahead of European monetary union.

INSEE said consumer spending would be one of the major motors of the economy all year. It said that, despite a forecast drop in consumption in the fourth quarter, consumption should rise 2.5 percent in 1996.

Its comments followed an INSEE consumer survey released on Thursday that showed household sentiment worsened in September, while fears of unemployment rose. Economists said the consumer gloom masked an actual pick up in spending.

"Despite very badly oriented earnings expectations and the rise in unemployment, household purchases have been particularly strong since the beginning of the year thanks to a sharp decline in the savings rate, supported by the drop in interest rates and a tax structure less favourable to savings," INSEE said.
Unemployment is currently at a record 12.6 percent.
INSEE said unemployment was likely continue to rise for the rest of the year, but at a slower pace. It saw the growth in jobs at just 1.1 percent this year after a rise of 2.9 percent last year.
A drawdown in stocks would slow through the year and companies would start restocking in the fourth quarter.
French economic recoveries have traditionally been driven by stock-building in recent years.

It said stocks, which fell by 9.3 billion francs in the first quarter, would fall by 4.7 billion and 4.5 billion in the second and third quarters, respectively, before rising by 1.4 billion in the fourth quarter.

In terms of contribution to GDP, these figures represented a negative 1.0 percent in the first quarter, followed by a positive 0.5 percent, 0.0 percent and 0.7 percent, respectively, in the second, third and fourth quarters.
Business investment should end flat for the year as corporations take a-wait-and-see attitude toward projects.
